purpose: Teach: 有利/他者/ロンドン/清水/余りに/不便/スケール/優位

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、商売で、絶対、有利、絶対、な、絶対、立場、絶対、保ったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, do you remember? When your father was young, he really held his own in business. He kept that edge, no matter what.
lines.style: Slow, reaching back into time. Gentle nostalgia on each memory. Pauses between phrases like he's turning pages. Quiet conviction—these are facts he knows she'll understand.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、他者、絶対、への、絶対、思いやり、絶対、深かったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: I do. And you know, your grandfather back then—he had such a deep kindness toward everyone around him. Do you remember that about him?
lines.style: Warm, almost singing the memory aloud. Eyes bright with recognition. Gentle insistence—she's not just answering, she's confirming what matters. Voice settles on the word 'kindness'.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、ロンドン、絶対、出張、絶対、よく行ったぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気for
lines.en: Gran, your father traveled to London all the time back then, remember? Business trips, constantly. He was always on the move.
lines.style: Fond exasperation in the cadence. The rhythm of someone describing a beloved restlessness. Slight lift on 'London'—the glamour and the weight of it. Checking her face for recognition.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、清水、絶対、寺、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、参拝したわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, dear. And I remember—your grandfather and I, we'd visit Kiyomizu Temple together back then. Those quiet mornings, just us.
lines.style: Soft and grounded. The voice of someone holding a specific memory like a stone in her palm. Tender on 'together.' Trails slightly—the weight of 'just us' hanging in the air.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、余りに、絶対、忙しくて、絶対、家に、絶対、いない日、絶対、多かったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Your father was so busy then, Gran. There were days—whole stretches—when he simply wasn't home. The business demanded everything from him.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact undercurrent, but the sadness is underneath, not performed. Even pacing. The word 'wasn't' gets a small emphasis—not bitter, just the fact of absence. Voice quiets at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、家、絶対、田舎で、絶対、不便、絶対、だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: The house was so far out in the countryside then. Everything was inconvenient, wasn't it? That was just how things were.
lines.style: Accepting, almost philosophical. No complaint—just acknowledgment of what was. Warm acceptance of the hardship. Voice settles into the rhythm of rural life, unhurried and real.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さんの、絶対、商売の、絶対、スケール、絶対、大きくなったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: His business grew so much, Gran. The scale of it, the reach—it all got so much bigger. You saw that happen, didn't you?
lines.style: Pride and wonder mixed together. Moderate pace, steady. The word 'bigger' carries weight—admiration for the ambition, respect for what he built. Seeking her confirmation like a shared victory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、業界で、絶対、優位、絶対、保ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: He did, dear. Your grandfather held his ground in that world—kept his advantage, kept his position. He knew how to do it.
lines.style: Affirming and sure. A note of recognition for competence, for holding steady. Quiet pride in the fact. Voice lands firmly on 'held his ground'—she knows what that cost.
